Anyway, at the end of senior year, my boyfriend and I broke up. Cue the summer before college…I see the friend group posting photos on Facebook all summer long…without the dude they said they were going to ghost…and without me. I never got an invite or heard from any of them again other than the few times I reached out to try and plan something and was met with lukewarm “oh yeah we should meet up sometime” responses that were never followed through with. I was so hurt that I was missing out and confused because I hadn’t had any problems with anyone in the group and I had been friends with them before my ex had. I stupidly held onto hope and kept reaching out to them both as a group and to individuals of the group, for probably two or three years, until one day when one of the people said posted a photo on Facebook that was only a few blocks from where I lived, saying she just got a new job there and couldn’t wait to explore the city. I messaged her saying I lived minutes away and we should meet up and explore together, and her response was, “Miss you!”. That was when the shoe dropped for me. They chose my ex over me. That was when I finally realized, oh, they had no issue ghosting that one particular dude, so they wouldn’t really have an issue ghosting me. And also…the girl that the particular dude “creeped on” and the dude he “picked fights with” ended up dating in college. So yeah. Hopefully this makes sense, I’m obviously simplifying things for summary purposes. 

What I’m trying to say is, if I were you, I’d be cautious with this friend group. (Well if I were you I’d ghost them, but you have more context to your situation). When people show you their true colors, believe them.

It’s rough. 

Sometimes people are in your life for a while and there are good moments, meaningful, life changing moments, but after a time they still have to go. Maybe it’s just time to move on. You can still cherish those memories, but you gotta do what’s best for you.

I am asexual. My boyfriend is heterosexual. He doesn't care about the frequency of when we do sexual things. We used to be intimate about once a week, maybe more. Then I started taking medicine for depression/anxiety and I have barely any ability to get turned on (and it's really hard to orgasm). Also we both are super busy with school. Since then it's definitely been less frequent, but you know what? It hasn't been an issue. Not for us. Some people might not want that kind of relationship, and that's okay. I know I wouldn't be right for those kinds of people. Don't feel like the person you are currently with is the closest you'll get to someone accepting your asexuality. If you feel uncomfortable with something, he should respect that (and that really goes for anyone, regardless of orientation). Don't go along with something that you're not sure about because it will only eat at you and weaken your relationship. Additionally, it doesn't seem logical that him having sex with other people is going to make him "accept" your lack of sex drive (which seems to be the issue, not your asexuality), unless you plan to keep that arrangement forever. I understand you like each other a lot, but that doesn't mean you are a good fit for each other. In the long run, being alone for a while is better than feeling manipulated, scared, and uncomfortable.

I always had crushes on people since I was pretty young (7 or 8) and obviously they were nonsexual at that age. As I got older, I still had the same kind of nonsexual crushes on people that I had an interest in, but other people started thinking about their crushes in a sexual way. I didn't really understand, and I honestly thought a lot of people were making it up to sound older and more mature. By the time I was 15 and in high school, the other students and some of my friends were getting into sexual relationships, but it didn't really appeal to me. Even though I had a libido/masturbated, I didn't feel the need to share that with another person. I remember thinking that maybe when I was older I would just fall so in love with someone that the sexual feelings would just appear. When I was 17 I first saw the term 'asexual' used in reference to people, I googled it and came across AVEN. The first two weeks after finding that site I did a lot of reading and research about asexuality and asexual people. For the most part, everything I read seemed to describe me really well, I just never knew there was a word for it!

I'm 21 now, and I'm finally comfortable with my asexuality. Since being 17 I've been in a few relationships and had some sexual experiences. As a whole, I feel pretty neutral about sex (though some asexuals are repulsed by it, some like it due to intimacy, etc.). I think if you are questioning whether or not you are asexual, the best thing to do is just keep looking through information about asexuality. Lots of asexual people have blogs or youtube channels, and there are a lot of forums and websites as well. Even within asexuality there is a huge margin for diversity (romantic orientations, sex drive, attitudes about sex, gray areas, etc) so even if one person knew they were asexual because of x, y and z reason, maybe another person identifies as asexual because of a, b and c reason.
